GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2018-10-19T13:59:02Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: 2.1.6 PublishProcessor.debounce() is interrupting previous operation.
Description: RxJava 2.1.6 in Android.

I have processor which offers a search text which is followed by debounce in order not to do search request each time a character of search phrase changes. I realized it doesn't work, when I type characters faster than BETWEEN_SEARCHES_INTERVAL = 300 millis. What is happening is that OkHttp throws interrupted exception from inside of searchRepository.searchInNetwork() method.

```
tRestFSOperation: java.io.InterruptedIOException: thread interrupted
tRestFSOperation:     at okio.Timeout.throwIfReached(Timeout.java:145)
tRestFSOperation:     at okio.Okio$2.read(Okio.java:137)
```

I guess that debounce is interrupting the thread on which previous emission is running. I think it's unintended behaviour. At least it's not documented.

```
    fun subscribeToSearch() {
        if (disposables.size() == 0) {
            disposables.add(
                searchPublishProcessor
                    .debounce(BETWEEN_SEARCHES_INTERVAL, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS, Schedulers.io())
                    // .throttleLast(BETWEEN_SEARCHES_INTERVAL, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS, Schedulers.io())
                    .distinctUntilChanged()
                    .filter { it.searchPhrase.isNotBlank() }
                    .flatMap {
                        searchForPhraseInFolder(it)
                    }
                    .subscribeOn(Schedulers.io())
                    .onErrorReturn { e: Throwable ->
                        Timber.w(e, "Error in search request")
                        SearchState.Builder(searchState)
                            .setState(LoadingState.ERROR)
                            .setException(Unique(e))
                            .build()

                    }
                    .observeOn(AndroidSchedulers.mainThread())
                    .subscribe({ newSearchState: SearchState? -> publishState(newSearchState!!) },
                        { e: Throwable? ->
                            Timber.e(e, "Error while search")
                            CrashInfo.submitHandledCrash(e, "SearchViewModel.search() broken")
                        }))
        }
    }

    private fun searchForPhraseInFolder(it: SearchQuery): Flowable<SearchState>? {
        return Flowable.fromCallable { searchRepository.searchInNetwork(it.searchPhrase, it.folderResourceId) }
            .map { resources: List<Resource> ->
                SearchState.Builder(searchState)
                    .setResources(resources)
                    .setState(if (resources.isEmpty()) LoadingState.EMPTY else LoadingState.DONE)
                    .build()
            }
            .startWith(
                SearchState.Builder(searchState)
                    .setState(LoadingState.LOADING)
                    .build()
            )
            .subscribeOn(Schedulers.io())
    }
```
